doc.title: Wayne Shorter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: What he listens for: struggle, victory and question marks
summary: He listens for struggle, victory and 'no beginning, no end'; asked about human nature creating resolution.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: When you listen to music or look at art or watch a film, what are you listening for, what are you watching, what are you looking at?

You know what I’m listening for? Struggle and victory. Struggle and victory and overcoming. Or also, there’s investigation. Or a question mark. A question mark in music... I’m listening for something that’s saying, “No beginning, no end.” The words “beginning” and “end” to me are like crutches, tools. They’re artificial. They’re to be used. Not to those ends, though. Or those beginnings. They’re to use, but not to use us.
Isn’t it human nature to create resolution?
